name: Cathedral Glass
summary: A living cathedral window: jewel-tone glass pieces in dark lead came, lit from behind by warm light and coloured rays.
description: The whole world is one backlit stained-glass window. Floor, props, characters, pickups, icons and even damage numbers are built from the same unit: a glass piece with a luminous off-centre core, a darker rim, faint streaks and a glint, separated by near-black lead came with a soft metallic ridge. Material regions (meadow, autumn leaf carpet, amber path, night glass, clear diamond quarries) are separated by heavier lead, and props cast coloured light pools onto the floor. It feels sacred, festive and handcrafted while staying readable because every actor has a fat lead silhouette.
avoidFor: fast-twitch shooters needing a calm background

difficulty.why: Every new figure has to be split sensibly into glass pieces and still stay readable; the ground is already visually busy.

technique.resolution: Native resolution. Actor and prop sprites are baked once at K = clamp(round(screenScale x 1.5), 3, 5) px per world unit; the ground is rendered per pixel in 256-unit chunks at up to 2.5 px per world unit.
technique.summary: Each figure is a list of parts drawn twice: an outline pass fills and strokes every part in lead (one fat outer came), then a fill pass clips glass pieces (BSP-cut polygons, rib lenses, half-leaves) into each part, shades each with an off-centre radial gradient and strokes inner lead. The ground is a per-pixel world-anchored Voronoi with an antialiased lead ramp.
technique.linework: Lead colour #17131c everywhere. Actors: outer came = 0.95 world units each side (lineWidth 1.9), inner lead 0.55 units, part borders 0.66 units, small faces/eyes use ol 0.4-0.6. Floor: piece lead half-width 0.78 units, region-border lead 1.2 units, with a lighter ridge (rgb 84,78,96) along the centre. lineJoin and lineCap round.
technique.shading: Per glass piece: radial gradient from (cx-0.25r, cy-0.3r) to centre, stops 0 = colour mixed 30% with white, 0.48 = base colour (±6% brightness jitter), 1 = colour x0.64. Glowing pieces (faces, eyes, jewels) use 78% warm white core and x0.9 rim. Floor pieces get luminance 0.6 at the lead rising to 0.98 at the centre (smoothstep over 0.34 x cell size).
technique.lighting: Backlit glass: light comes through the window, not from a direction. Warm additive glow sprites behind carved faces, candles and gems; coloured elliptical light pools under props (additive, alpha 0.1-0.3); a screen layer of five coloured diagonal light rays plus a warm centre, added with 'lighter' and slowly drifting.
technique.texture: Cathedral-glass streaks (two curved white strokes at 12% alpha per piece), elliptical glints on half the pieces, sinusoidal ripple banding in floor pieces (±5.5%), seedy bubbles in clear quarries, scattered diagonal white glint strokes on the floor and faint screen-anchored wavy ripple lines.

palette.name: Lead came
palette.role: All outlines, piece seams, text strokes, UI borders

palette.name: Lead ridge
palette.role: Soft metallic highlight in the middle of floor lead lines

palette.name: Meadow green
palette.role: Main floor glass (with #327a4e, #265f44, #3a8250, #2a7058, #2f6c40), ~45% of the screen

palette.name: Hem gold
palette.role: Clasps, hems, fruit jewels, star decals

palette.name: Window gold fillet
palette.role: Thin gold ring inside every UI lead border

paletteRules: Every colour is a saturated jewel tone at mid value; pure white and pure black never appear as surface colour (only lead #17131c and highlight mixes).
Lead is the only dark: roughly 12-18% of floor pixels are lead. Never draw a glass piece darker than its colour x0.6.
Background regions use cool or earthy mid tones (greens, crimson, blue, grey); actors use brighter, warmer or paler pieces (orange, ivory, opal, amethyst) so they pop against the floor.
Anything that 'emits' (faces, eyes, flames, gems, cores) uses glow pieces: warm-white core plus an additive glow sprite. Reserve gold/yellow for these and for UI numbers.
Each region picks a random swatch per piece from a 5-7 colour family with ±7% brightness; never use a single flat colour for a whole area.

typography.role: Titles, clock, counters, damage numbers, level-up heading
typography.css: font: 900 34px/1.05 'Cinzel Decorative', 'Cinzel', serif; letter-spacing: 2px; color: #ffdf7e; text-shadow: 2.5px 0 0 #17131c, -2.5px 0 0 #17131c, 0 2.5px 0 #17131c, 0 -2.5px 0 #17131c, 0 0 14px rgba(255,200,90,.7);

typography.role: Body text, labels, HP text, card descriptions
typography.css: font: 700 11px/1 'Cinzel', Georgia, serif; letter-spacing: 3px; color: #cfdaff; text-shadow: 0 1px 2px #17131c;

background.summary: A per-pixel, world-anchored stained-glass floor. Smooth noise fields decide the material region; each material is a jittered-grid Voronoi tessellation (cell 15-30 units) whose seams and region borders become antialiased lead with a metallic ridge. Leaded glass decals (flowers, leaves, stars, roundels) and glints are drawn on top, then prop light pools.
layers: Material field: 5 noise layers sampled on a 4-unit grid, bilinear value / bilinear gradient = signed distance in world units; priority plaza > path (|d| < 21) > night > leaf carpet > meadow.
Voronoi glass per material: meadow cell 20, leaf carpet 15, night 23, path 30 (3 lanes split at ±7 units), plaza = 45° diamond quarries every 17 units.
Per-piece shading: luminance 0.6 at the lead to 0.98 in the middle, sinusoidal streak ±5.5%, macro brightness from a 1150-unit noise.
Lead: piece seams half-width 0.78, region borders 1.2, colour ramp from rgb(28,24,34) at the edge to rgb(84,78,96) at the centre ridge.
Decals: leaded flowers (5 petals) on meadow, autumn leaves on the carpet, gold stars on night glass, amber roundels on the path, seedy bubbles on quarries.
Glints: short diagonal white strokes at 20% alpha scattered every ~24 units.
Prop contact shadows (rgba(16,12,24,0.38)) and additive coloured light pools.

characters.summary: Chunky, chibi figures (hero 1.15 x ~21 units wide, ~36 tall incl. stem) assembled from 10-25 glass pieces: pumpkin heads from 5 vertical rib lenses, clothes from BSP-cut mosaics, leaves from two half-pieces split on the midrib, carved faces as glowing gold polygons. Pre-rendered in 4 walk frames plus a 'flash' (lit glass) copy of each frame.
rules: Every figure has one fat outer lead came (1.9 units wide) from the outline pass, so silhouettes read on the busy floor.
Faces and eyes are glow pieces (warm-white core) plus an additive glow sprite: the face is the brightest thing on any actor.
Pieces get smaller where detail matters (face, hands) and larger on bodies; never more than ~25 pieces on a small actor.
Actors are warmer, paler or more saturated than the floor region they stand on.
Facing = horizontal flip of the baked sprite; carved faces are drawn offset 1.5 units towards the facing side.
Hit flash = blit the pre-baked flash copy (pieces mixed 58% toward warm white, lead kept) at alpha <= 0.62 over the normal sprite.
Death = enemy shatters into 6-16 leaded shards in its own colours; spawn = shards fly in and assemble.

effects.name: Shatter
effects.how: On kill, 6 (ghost), 8 (small) or 16 (brute) shard sprites: 3 baked triangle/quad shapes with lead outline, coloured from the enemy palette. They fly out with gravity 300, drag 1.4, life 0.9-1.4 s, spin ±8 rad/s and fake 3D tumble by scaling y with |cos|; when edge-on they flash a glint.

effects.name: Hit glint
effects.how: Four-point star sprite (white core, tinted halo, curved spikes 7.5 units) added with 'lighter', scale ramps in over 30% of life then out; 45% chance of a single shard.

effects.name: Seed projectile
effects.how: A two-piece leaded seed sprite rotated to its heading, y-scale 0.6-1 by spin, with a 16-unit additive tapered trail (rgba 255,214,120 .75 to 0) and a small gold glow.

effects.name: Glow sprites
effects.how: Radial gradients baked once (stops 0:0.9, 0.25:0.45, 0.6:0.12, 1:0 alpha) in warm, gold, aqua, cold and ruby, blitted with globalCompositeOperation 'lighter' behind faces, gems, candles and brute cores.

effects.name: Level-up beams
effects.how: 12 vertical light beams (3.2 x 40 units, gradient 0 / 0.7 / 0 with a white 0.8-unit core) in gold, rose, blue and mint around the hero plus a lead-and-gold expanding ellipse ring.

effects.name: Ring shockwave
effects.how: Ellipse ring (ry = 0.45 rx) stroked twice: lead at width w+1.4, then the colour additively at width w = 2.6 x (1-t).

effects.name: Damage numbers
effects.how: Cinzel Decorative 900 at 9.2 units (12.5 crit), stroked twice in lead (width 0.26 x font size, once offset down), filled with a vertical gradient (crit #fff6c0 > #ffcf40 > #ff7a1a, normal #ffffff > #e6eeff > #a9c0ee), white 50% band over the top; pop 0.4 > 1.25 > 1.

ui.summary: HUD pieces are leaded glass panels: thick lead borders (3-5 px) with a 2 px gold fillet ring, radial-gradient jewel glass fills, gothic arch tops on the clock, counter and level-up cards, bars with lead mullions every 40-46 px and a white highlight strip. Text is Cinzel / Cinzel Decorative with a 12-direction lead text-shadow outline.

motion: 4 baked walk frames per actor; hero cycles at 0.42 x distance, small enemy at 0.85, brute at 0.32; frame = floor(phase x 4) & 3.
Hero walk: lift |sin(phase x TAU)| x 2.2 units, rock ±0.05 rad, y-squash ±2%; idle breath ±2.5% y / ∓1.5% x at 3 rad/s.
Small enemy hops: lift |sin| x 1.2 units and rocks ±0.09 rad. Ghost floats 4 units up, bobs ±1.5 at 2.4 rad/s, tilts with velocity up to 0.14 rad, 6 fps frames, alpha 0.86.
Brute stomps: lift 1.8 units, contact squash (1-up)^4 x 5%.
Glows flicker with products of two sines (e.g. sin(9t) x sin(5.3t)); candle flames 0.75 + 0.25 sin(11t) sin(7.3t).
Trees and bushes sway as a horizontal skew of 0.02-0.03 at 1.1 rad/s; the screen light rays drift ±2.5% of the width at 0.12 rad/s.
Hit flash decays from 1 to 0; death is a 0.22 s flash-copy pop (scale 1 to 1.18, fading) followed by shards; spawn assembles shards over 0.85 s.
do: Draw every actor in two passes: a lead outline pass first, then the glass pieces with inner lead.
Give each glass piece its own off-centre radial gradient (light core, dark rim) and brightness jitter.
Split shapes where a real glazier would: pumpkin ribs, leaf midribs, cloak folds, facets of a gem.
Make faces, eyes, flames and jewels glow pieces plus an additive glow sprite.
Anchor the floor tessellation in world space and separate material regions with heavier lead.
Cast coloured additive light pools from props onto the floor.
Pre-bake every sprite and a lit 'flash' copy at init; blit at runtime.
Keep the overlay: vignette, lead window frame with gold fillet and slow coloured light rays.
dont: Don't use flat fills without lead seams; it instantly becomes generic vector art.
Don't flash enemies pure white: the flash copy keeps the lead and only lights the glass.
Don't make floor pieces as small as actor pieces; floor cells are 15-30 units, actor pieces 2-8 units.
Don't use thin or coloured outlines; lead is always the same near-black #17131c.
Don't add drop shadows with hard offsets or realistic directional lighting.
Don't use dark or desaturated actor colours on the same-hued region (e.g. green enemies on meadow).
Don't compute the per-pixel ground every frame; bake it in chunks.
performance: All actor/prop/icon sprites (hero 4 frames x2, 3 small-enemy variants x4 frames x2, ghost and brute 4x2, props, shards, glows) are baked once at init at 3-5 px per unit. The ground is the hot spot: per-pixel field bilinear + 3x3 Voronoi search + lead ramp, done as a time-sliced generator per 256-unit chunk at up to 2.5 px/unit and cached. Per frame: only drawImage blits, a handful of additive glow blits and two overlay drawImages (overlay baked per screen size, light layer at half resolution). Hundreds of enemies are fine because each is one or two blits.
